notes: The trend analysis is adjusted for race/ethnicity, sex and grade, implying a model whose family is not named (NYTS trend analyses are usually logistic). Comparison leads with group because the Summary gives both 2015–2016 pair contrasts and 2011–2016 trends. Discussion attributes overall declines to tobacco control policies, not tied to social position.
view_issues: Sex and race/ethnicity 'higher' claims have no stated test (t-tests are only for 2015 vs 2016). Text says e-cigarettes 11.3% 'of current users' but table gives 11.3% of all students. Table male cigar CI 9.0 (8.6–11.2) looks wrong. Figure notes call ≥2-product HS trend a nonlinear change; text says nonlinear decrease.
